brief: Flash September PMIs hit five-year highs, with S&P Global calling the improvement in business activity the best since early 2015 excluding the COVID reopening, though the note flags a possible nominal-bias distortion in the survey levels. Weak demand at a 5-year Treasury auction accelerated a bond selloff: yields hit a 4-sigma move, the biggest 10-year jump since Liberation Day and just two weeks after a 3-sigma spike. The 5-year and 10-year broke above 5.00% (5-year first time since 2007), the 30-year hit its highest since 2004, and mortgage rates topped 7%. Bloomberg estimates 80 to 85% of the move is real-rate repricing rather than an inflation scare. Swaps now price three Fed hikes over the next year plus hedging for a fourth, reinforced by Governor Barr's hawkish remarks and a note that Fed history shows midterms rarely stall tightening. Higher yields lifted the dollar to its highest since July, pushed gold below $4,300 and bitcoin to $84,000, and hit small caps and market breadth, while separately a proposed temporary US diesel export ban crashed US diesel futures and lifted EU diesel futures against a backdrop of fresh Hormuz attacks and record physical oil tightness.
